title: Longest Binary Subsequence Less Than or Equal to K
summary: Given a binary string and a positive integer k, find the length of the longest subsequence of the binary string that forms a binary number less than or equal to k.
statement: Given a binary string and a positive integer k, find the length of the longest subsequence of the binary string that forms a binary number less than or equal to k. The subsequence may include leading zeros, and an empty string is considered zero.
constraints: Choose a subsequence while preserving character order.
Interpret the chosen bits as a binary integer; leading zeroes are allowed.
Return the maximum subsequence length whose value is at most k.
hints: Every zero can be included because leading zeroes do not increase the value.
The cheapest one bits are at the rightmost positions, so inspect bits from right to left.
Include a one only when adding its place value keeps the total at most k; count all zeroes.
Exchanging any selected higher-place one for an available lower-place one cannot increase value, proving the greedy choice.
editorial: Exchanging any selected higher-place one for an available lower-place one cannot increase value, proving the greedy choice.

tests.explanation: All zeroes plus selected low-place one bits form a length-five value no greater than five.
Five zeroes and the final one form a valid length-six subsequence.
